nodes.body:
Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Low impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; no new actionable defect was established.

Summary

This PR updates NCCL setup and shutdown in two distributed test suites. - Fusible-ops runs finish their shared work before closing the process group. - Cross-entropy workers tell NCCL which CUDA device to use. The earlier cleanup finding is addressed: the barrier runs only after the tests succeed, and `finally` does not call `world_group()`. The unnumbered thread was manually resolved by `timmoon10` without an explanatory reply. Reviews (3) · Last reviewed commit: ["Apply suggestion from @timmoon10"](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/cf9201f91dfb009e14a9e643a54a7a113cf989ed) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_expert&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=code_reviews&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**Cleanup hangs after test failures** The `finally` block calls `barrier()` even when a test fails on just one rank. Passing ranks can enter the next test's collective instead, so their work no longer matches the failed rank's barrier. This can hang until NCCL times out, delay the original failure, and prevent `destroy_process_group()` from running. Keep the barrier on the success path. Put guarded destruction in `finally`, without calling `world_group()` during cleanup.
